chunks: Al-Tatari narrated from Ibn Ziyad, from Hammad, from Nu'man al-Razi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who missed some of the prayers and remembered them at sunrise and at sunset. He said: 'Let him pray when he remembered them.'

key_terms.اَلصَّلَوَاتِ: prayers (plural, often referring to the five daily obligatory prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed prayers if remembered at sunrise or sunset?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the timing for *Qada* (making up) missed obligatory prayers, ruling that they are performed immediately upon remembrance rather than being delayed until the next prayer time. This establishes the principle of *Fawr* (promptness) in fulfilling missed duties, distinguishing it from the specific times for *Adhkar* (remembrance) of the sun's rising and setting, which serve as the trigger for the obligation to act. The ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on timely rectification of worship to maintain spiritual continuity.
